clue.text: Sort we compare to round-dodging drunk

definitions.text: Sort we compare to round-dodging drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order
dodging a round means avoiding the ring-shaped letter, so that letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its round letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone at the bar is likened to the drinker who always slips away before it is their turn to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: TO loses its O (the round), then SORT WE COMPARE T is mixed up. The whole clue is the definition: a lightweight who leaves after two drinks dodges a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-pot screamer is Australian slang for a person who gets drunk on very little alcohol, the sort who is gone before buying a round.

clue.text: Prone to intermittent leaks, kept mum in case

indicators.note: something that leaks now and then loses every other drop, so only every second letter of the phrase survives

parts.note: the even-numbered letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A container that keeps dribbling has had its faults hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'in' does double work: it closes the fodder 'kept mum in' and also joins it to the definition 'case'. 'Kept mum' looks like secrecy but just supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for holding needles, scissors or cosmetics.

clue.text: So close, having exchanged tips

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters, and exchanging them rearranges it

parts.note: to close a door is to shut it

explanation.surface: Someone was so nearly there, after trading the ends of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the outer letters swap places; the middle two stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus and so are interchangeable adverbs meaning in this way or therefore.

clue.text: FC Flora's home wingers missing testimonial, as I am

indicators.note: the wingers of a word are its outermost letters, and here they are absent
'as I am' means the pronoun and verb are also missing, just like the outside letters

parts.note: taken as written
I am contracted to I'M

explanation.surface: A football club's wide players skip a veteran's benefit match, and so does the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first and last letters of TESTIMONIAL, then remove I'M as well. A testimonial in football is a benefit match for a long-serving player.
explanation.definitionFit: FC Flora is a football club based in Tallinn, the capital of Estonia, so the country is its home.

clue.text: Tar has caught cold on windy moor

indicators.note: a windy place blows things about, so the letters before it are tossed into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor picks up a chill out on a blustery stretch of upland.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word before 'windy' is fodder, including 'on'. 'Moor' looks like the bleak moorland but is the verb used of ships.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a ship is to secure it in place, which is what dropping its anchor does.

clue.text: Superman uniform, shade of blue, being adorned with merch pants!

indicators.note: 'pants' is slang for rubbish, signalling that the preceding word is garbled
something adorned has decoration wrapped around it, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: a shade is only a hint of a colour, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of blue
the letters of merch, mixed up and split around the next piece
ens is the philosophical Latin word for a being or existence

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero's blue costume is splashed with tacky merchandise on his trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hero is Superman of the comics; the definition is Nietzsche's ideal man, whose German name is usually translated as superman.
explanation.definitionFit: Übermensch is Nietzsche's German term, usually translated as superman, for an ideal superior human.

clue.text: Intro from this musical group slipped in by Halloween party?

indicators.note: things slipped in are inserted into what follows, so the earlier pieces go inside

parts.note: by and with both mean beside or by means of

indicators.note: the intro of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of this
Chess is the 1980s stage musical written by Tim Rice and two members of ABBA
ABBA is the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A song's opening and a band are sneaked into a spooky celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical and the group are linked: Chess was written by Benny Andersson and Björn Ulvaeus of the Swedish band. 'By' is the container itself, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A witches' sabbath is a midnight gathering of witches, and Halloween is the night famed for such a party; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: He/she might burn out rockers, but not for long

indicators.note: 'burn out' suggests something wrecked, and 'out' here means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the letters of these words, ignoring the slash

explanation.surface: Any rocker, of either sex, risks burning out before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn out' looks like a phrase about exhaustion; 'burn' is fodder and 'out' alone is the signal. The High Numbers was the band's name only briefly in 1964 before they became The Who.
explanation.definitionFit: The High Numbers were a rock band whose name lasted only a few months before they were renamed The Who.

clue.text: Price offered for horse painting left misery

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds offered on a racehorse
oils are paintings done in oil paint
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: The odds on a horse in a painting left someone feeling miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misery' looks like a feeling, but it is a person: a misery is a gloomy killjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A misery is informal British for a moaning person who dampens fun, which is what a spoilsport is.

clue.text: "Wild cat" her Valentine's signature?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a fierce feline quoted as a nickname
setter's reading: a woman signs her card with her name and a kiss, and name plus kiss reads as a wild cat

explanation.surface: A girl signs her Valentine card with a playful nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: A kiss on a card is written X; the woman's name followed by X spells the wild cat LYNX, so her name is LYN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyn is a woman's name, and 'Lyn x' as a signature looks just like the name of the wild feline.

clue.text: Republican vote for Old Overholt & co

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
a vote in favour is a yes

explanation.surface: A party member casts a vote for an old person or firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Overholt looks like a person's name, but it is a brand of American rye whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryes are rye whiskeys, and Old Overholt is one of the oldest American brands, so it and its kind are ryes.

clue.text: Direct route from Selby to Gateshead?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to point or steer something at a target
second meaning: the A1(M) motorway, read with the figure one as the letter I and the brackets dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The A1(M) is the motorway stretch of England's Great North Road that runs north past Selby towards Gateshead; the question mark admits the 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim something is to direct it towards a target, and the road label looks like the word once its digit passes for a letter.

clue.text: Party people still standing

parts.note: a stag is a men-only party before a wedding
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Revellers are still on their feet at the end of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still standing' reads as survivors of a party, but it means standing still.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is the condition of not moving or flowing, the state of standing still.

clue.text: Worry about parcels on my order from two parts of Europe

indicators.note: to parcel something up is to wrap it, so the reversed word wraps around the rest
turned about means facing the other way, so the word for worry is read backwards

parts.note: to nag is to worry or pester
re means on or concerning
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Someone frets over packages ordered from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor' is a mild British exclamation meaning 'my!' or 'gosh!', and 'on' meaning 'concerning' is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Greco-Roman describes something belonging to both ancient Greece and Rome, two regions of Europe.

clue.text: Jack's behind ex-Gold Coast clothing firm's cutting winter wear

indicators.note: clothing something means dressing it, so the first piece wraps around what follows

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and aft is the sailor's word for behind

indicators.note: something cutting into another is inserted inside it

parts.note: Ghana was the British colony called the Gold Coast
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A sailor stands behind a West African garment company that is slashing its winter range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack's' means 'Jack is', with Jack a sailor. The firm cuts into the country just before its last letter, and the stern word wraps the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afghan coat is a sheepskin coat with the fleece inside, worn against the cold.

clue.text: Appeal that was, perhaps, way out

parts.note: ex is the prefix for a former thing
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A court appeal that once happened was perhaps far-fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal that was' is a former appeal, so the prefix for former comes first. 'Way out' suggests outlandish but is a door sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a way out of a building, as the sign above the door announces.

clue.text: Large-scale spread? Not always large or small

indicators.note: spread about suggests letters scattered and laid out again in a new pattern
'not always' read as not at any point means every such letter must go

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A big spread need not be large; sometimes it is small.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both Ls and the S from LARGE-SCALE and mix what is left. 'Spread' does double duty as the anagram signal and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a farm or ranch with its land, and acreage is the extent of land measured in acres.

clue.text: Book group (8), but missing the show, sadly

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so the following word is taken away

parts.note: the band in 8 down later took the name The Who
taken as written, to be removed

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reading club misses the performance, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: The group from 8 down is The Who; drop THE and add a jumbled SHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Who's Who is a reference book listing biographies of notable people.

clue.text: Moves data describing aviation fanatic?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sends files from a device to a server
second meaning, split 2-5: someone who loves flying likes being in the air a great deal

explanation.walkthrough: Split as UP LOADS, the answer describes a flying enthusiast who is aloft lots of the time; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Uploads are transfers of files onto a remote computer, so the verb means shifting data.

clue.text: Writer given second reminder

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to the setter, me
mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: An author is handed another note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second reminder' reads as a follow-up note, but 'second' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note serving as a reminder.

clue.text: Some charge for every pardon in love

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: amour is a love affair
per means for each
eh? asks someone to repeat, like pardon?

explanation.surface: Each charge is forgiven in the name of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks legal or financial but is electrical, and 'love' is the French word rather than the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampere hour is a unit of electric charge, the amount carried by one ampere flowing for an hour.

clue.text: The answer is here in the written word

definitions.text: The answer is here in the written word

indicators.note: the solution itself says where to look: at the final letter of each following word

parts.note: the last letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone points out that the solution can be found in print.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer tells you where to look: the last letters of the final three words. Read whole, the clue also says the answer sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The end is the final part of something, and that is exactly where this answer's letters lie in the clue.

clue.text: Managed a single marathon?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one ... scored in cricket
third meaning: a long race on foot, by example

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the past participle sense of managing, a single scored in cricket, and a marathon as an example of a long jog, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word covers having managed something, one cricket score and a race on foot such as a marathon.

clue.text: Boss fleeced dimwits

indicators.note: a fleeced sheep has lost its outer coat, so the outside letters are stripped away

parts.note: dumbos are stupid people

explanation.surface: A manager cheated some fools out of their money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but it is the raised centre of a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbo is the round projecting knob at the centre of a shield, also called its boss.

clue.text: Top hat in America and China

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head or of a hat
derby is the American name for a bowler hat

explanation.surface: A top hat is worn in the United States and in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' reads as the country beside America, but it is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby is a famous English porcelain maker, so its tableware is a kind of fine china.

clue.text: An absence of American intellect

parts.note: no means none, an absence
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a lack of brains in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nous' is British informal for common sense or practical intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous comes from the Greek for mind and means good sense or intelligence.

clue.text: A little sustenance at supper-time?

indicators.note: a little of something is only a part of it, so the letters are found inside the following words

parts.note: letters running across these words

explanation.surface: A light snack served in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of 'sustenance', all of 'at' and the start of 'supper'; read whole, the clue describes the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, which is the sustenance served at supper.

clue.text: Means study in second-class state

indicators.note: in places the word for study inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: Band B is the second grade in a ranking of classes
to read a subject is to study it at university
to utter is to say or state

explanation.surface: A student's resources are studied in a lowly region.
explanation.walkthrough: The study word goes in after the first letter of the two-part phrase, and 'state' follows. 'Means' looks like a verb but is the noun for a livelihood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread and butter is one's basic livelihood, the means by which one earns a living.
